findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: called from the invoice loop (src/report.rs:23-26, `customer: customer_label(db, invoice)?`), `monthly_report` runs `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice, so a month of about 3 000 invoices (proposal) costs about 3 000 sequential round trips for only 800 distinct customers; the cost grows linearly with the month's invoices. `Db` already offers `customers(&[i64])` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`, src/db.rs:26): collect the distinct `customer_id`s, fetch them in one call, index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>` and build each label from it, keeping the invoice order and returning the same error when a customer is missing.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called once per invoice in the report loop (src/report.rs:28) and compiles the same pattern on each call, so a month of about 3 000 invoices compiles it about 3 000 times; compiling a regex is far more expensive than matching one short note. Compile it once, in a `static PATTERN: std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `OnceLock`), and reuse it.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled again for every invoice
